value.body: Builds both the visible side of a web app (frontend) and the server, database and APIs behind it (backend), so a feature can be delivered end to end. The role is common in startups and small product teams, and also exists in IT services firms and GCCs. A day may move between a user-interface change, a database query and a deployment fix.

items.label: Common tools
items.value: JavaScript/TypeScript, Node.js, Java or Python, SQL databases, Git, cloud basics

items.label: Indian tech-sector workforce
items.note: Whole IT-BPM sector, not this role alone

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Many start as frontend or backend developers and widen their scope; others join a startup that expects broad skills from day one. A couple of complete, deployed projects — with login, a database and an API — is the clearest proof at interviews. Campus placement into IT services is the most common first job.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript and a framework
Backend APIs in Node.js, Java or Python
Deployment basics — Linux, cloud, CI pipelines

value.title: At a glance
items: Growth path: developer → senior → tech lead or architect.
Breadth can come at the cost of depth; many specialise later.
Startups use the title loosely, so job descriptions vary widely.
